page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and driven by a 48-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V with simultaneous multithreading, the system provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4:1 memory-to-core allocation. Storage provisions include a dedicated 5,670 GB local NVMe SSD, while discrete GPU hardware is not included.

Benchmark results place the instance in high performance tiers for multi-threaded and vector operations. The platform achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,967.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 86,698.13, aided by integrated Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets. Memory testing indicates read bandwidth reaching 257.11 GB/sec on uncached 256MB blocks, supporting operational throughput of 107.53 million Redis SET operations per second and 116.39 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

Cost efficiency is supported through high compute density and large integrated NVMe storage, which mitigates reliance on external block devices for temporary data. The memory allocation follows standard general-purpose ratios rather than high-memory profiles, and the absence of hardware accelerators constrains complex deep learning training. The server architecture is technically aligned with high-concurrency relational databases, large in-memory caches, software compilation tasks, and enterprise web delivery.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v6 is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores via an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it contains 384.0 GB of memory and 5,670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. Multi-core performance is confirmed by a Geekbench score of 21,967.0 and a PassMark rating of 86,698.13, supported by AVX-512 and AMX extensions. High-throughput data processing capabilities are reflected in 107.53 million Redis SET operations per second and 116.39 GB/sec in static web delivery. The inclusion of multi-terabyte NVMe storage offers low-latency local I/O without incurring external block storage overhead for scratch operations. This configuration addresses enterprise relational databases, distributed caching layers, automated build infrastructure, and intensive web serving deployments.
